key_insight: CareMirror reframes dementia care by treating caregiver wellbeing as a core part of the care ecosystem, not an afterthought. It proposes connected tools that help caregivers reflect over time, receive personalized support, and share information with clinicians on their own terms.
problem_solved: Family caregivers of people with dementia often carry heavy emotional and practical burdens, but their wellbeing is rarely tracked or supported within clinical dementia care. This paper addresses the gap between caregiver needs and the care system by designing a way to surface caregiver wellbeing longitudinally and support coordinated care.
method: Built CareMirror as an envisioned caregiver wellbeing ecosystem with caregiver-facing and clinician-facing interfaces.
Used CareMirror as a design probe in semi-structured interviews with 14 caregivers to explore needs, workflows, and acceptable sharing practices.
Focused on longitudinal reflection, personalized support, and caregiver-controlled information sharing with clinical care.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work highlights that useful systems are not only predictive or diagnostic—they can also support human-centered coordination, reflection, and trust. It is especially relevant for designing AI-enabled health tools that respect privacy, agency, and caregiver burden.
visual_elements: A two-panel ecosystem diagram showing caregiver and clinician interfaces connected through a shared wellbeing layer.
A longitudinal timeline chart illustrating caregiver reflections, stress levels, and support interventions over time.
An icon-based flow showing data capture, reflection, personalization, and caregiver-controlled sharing.
A relationship map of caregiver, patient, and clinician roles with information boundaries and touchpoints.
paper_title: CareMirror: Bringing Caregiver Wellbeing into the Dementia Care Ecosystem
paper_authors: Jiayue Melissa Shi, Ethan Nguyen, Drishti Goel, Upasana Natarajan, Shashwat Srivatsa
